## My request:
### Objective

Add new MIDI parts to your song and edit them. If you need some ideas, you can try duplicating your bass guitar recording with synth bass. Replacing or enhancing your kick and snare is also a common technique. Try and see if your arrangement can benefit from synth pads or string parts. Submit the latest version of your song in **WAV** format.

### Requirements

1. **Record a Live MIDI Track:** Using a MIDI keyboard, or a drum pad, or your DAW's musical typing interface, record at least one new instrument track in real time (e.g., synth pads, strings, or keys).
2. **Program/Sequence a MIDI Track:** Manually program or sequence at least one separate MIDI track without live tracking (e.g., drawing in a drum groove or a step-input bassline).
3. **Quantize Your Timing:** Apply timing quantization to at least one MIDI track (new or existing) to snap the performances to your project grid.
4. **Edit Note Velocities:** Open the MIDI editor or piano roll window for at least one track and modify note velocities to create natural, human-sounding dynamics and accents.
5. **Finalize the Tracking Phase:** This week marks your final opportunity to complete your recordings before moving to the mixing phase. Verify that your arrangement contains the mandatory baseline instrumentation:
   - Lead Vocals
   - Backing Vocals (optional)
   - Drums and Bass
   - At least one primary Harmonic Instrument (Guitar or Keys)
   - At least one Melodic Instrument/Part (Synth lead, strings, or an instrumental solo track)

### Deliverables

1. File Uploads
   - **Audio File:** Export your completed full arrangement as a high-resolution **24-bit / 48 kHz stereo WAV file.**
   - **Screenshot:** Attach a screenshot showing the MIDI work you did this week. This can be a screenshot of the edit (arranger) and MIDI editor (piano roll) windows.
2. Text Submission\
   Use the text box on this page and type out a brief response detailing these two points:
   - Identify which MIDI track was performed live and which track was step-programmed. And your MIDI edits.
   - Any other changes, new recordings, parts, etc.
3. File Naming Conventions
   - **Audio File:** *Assignment7_MIDI_FirstInitialLastName.wav*
